notes: Precedence: command line, then config file, then defaults. The config file is one JSON object with 'version': 2 and only the top-level keys version, server, engine, models; a wrong block or an unknown name stops the start.

Keys are flag names without dashes; config.py also accepts underscores and any case (max_context == max-context) and strips a leading --. Switches are JSON true/false (a false switch simply omits the flag). A list value gives a flag several values, one word per item.
Repeatable server options take a list in the file: allowed-host, cors-origin, image-url-host, image-dir (and the undocumented script).

command_line_only: 'api-key' (any key whose letters start with 'apikey' is refused in every block; an empty key is an error) and 'config'. --model and --alias cannot be combined with --config. 'engine-bin' cannot be set in a file (it is set by 'basalt serve').
Paths for 'model', 'tokenizer' and 'image-dir' are resolved relative to the config file; other paths as given.

Where the docs mark a setting Flash-Next only or DeepSeek only: given in a model entry or on the command line of the other model it stops the start; in the top-level engine block it is left out for that model with a start line.

The docs' 'entry' location is also accepted in the top-level 'engine' block (config.py MODEL_OPTIONS): every entry-scoped server option (gpu, vision, parallel, slot-full-context, idle-sleep, idle-unload, min-free-vram-mib, fit-max-tokens, grammar, the reasoning settings, the sampling defaults) can be set once for all models under 'engine'. A model entry's own value wins over 'engine'.

Contradiction: gpus.md says 'gpu' can go in the config's 'server' section, but config.py refuses it there ('a model setting, set it under "engine" or in a model entry'). Use entry or top-level engine.

parallel sets the engine's --batch/--slots itself and stops the start if --batch or --slots is also given; with parallel > 1 and no slot-full-context, max-context is divided per slot (at least 256 tokens per slot).

Automatic settings: when left out the engine picks peer-exclusive, resident (reported as ram-experts; the budget key is resident-budget-gib; there is no separate 'resident' catalog entry), pool-affinity and pool-workers. A given value always wins.

From diagnostics.md the engine/serve measurement flags are included (real engine keys, all off by default and 'not settings' in the docs); one-shot CLI flags (--tokens, --max-new, --greedy, --stats, --no-pool, ...), basalt-bench/basalt-device flags, --gpu-plan (it prints the GPU plan and exits) and request-level keys (ppl=, ppl_t=, relaxed_drafting) are not config settings and are not cataloged.

Checked against bin/basalt.exe 0.3.2 (tools/audit_scopes.py): every catalog key is a name basalt itself uses. One exception found and dropped: diagnostics.md lists --diag-tier-frozen, which this build's engine does not carry; the documented --diag-tier-ram is cataloged in its place, and the undocumented --diag-tier-vram is left out.

blocks.server: Options shared by the whole server: listen address and port, Host/CORS/payload limits, image-source allow-lists, logging and the mock-engine test aids.
blocks.engine: Top-level block of engine flags and entry-scoped server options applied to every model that takes them; a model entry's own value wins, and a flag a model lacks is skipped for it with a start line.
blocks.entry: One object in 'models': 'model' and optional 'alias' plus that model's own server options (gpu, vision, parallel, idle, sampling defaults, ...) and its own engine flags.

settings.summary: The .basalt file (weights, tokenizer, chat template, drafter, vision projector and default sampling); required, path relative to the config file; entry only, never the engine block.
The model name the API reports, defaulting to the name stored in the file; two identical aliases stop the start.
Listen address; 0.0.0.0 serves the network, never without api-key.
The TCP port to listen on.
Require this key on /v1/* (Authorization: Bearer or x-api-key); command line only, cannot go in a file, and an empty key is refused.
The config file itself; command line only.
Also answer to this Host name (repeatable, so a list in the file); "*" turns the check off.
Let web pages from this origin call /v1/* (repeatable, so a list in the file).
Open the web page in the browser once the model is ready.
Start unloaded and load on the first request; a sidecar image encoder is dropped, vision dynamic stays.
One log line per request, and the raw model text.
Echo the per-request summary on stdout.
Largest request body the server reads, in MiB; a bigger one gets a 413; must be at least 1.
Clamp max_tokens to the remaining context instead of answering 400.
Unload the model after this many seconds idle (unset = off), freeing VRAM for other programs; the next request loads it again.
Sleep after this many seconds idle: VRAM freed, RAM kept, wake in seconds; Linux only, so off the table for a Windows host.
Load an unloaded model only when this much VRAM is free, else answer 503; unset = off.
Hold tool calls and JSON formats (json_object, json_schema) to their schema inside the engine (off with false / --no-grammar); without it, other JSON formats are refused with 400.
Default thinking budget for requests that name none (0 = none); a request's own value wins; keep it below the request's max_tokens.
End the thinking and let the model answer when one token repeats this many times in a row inside the thinking; 0 turns it off.

Reserve room for closing the thinking and the answer when the output cap is at least 1,024 tokens (off with false / --no-answer-room; an explicit request budget of 0 opts out). From basalt 0.3.3 there is no --no-answer-room and a false here stops the start: the value is a number or auto.

settings.default: the model file's sampling, else the engine's
settings.summary: Default temperature for requests that leave it out; 0 is greedy, higher is more random; a request's field always wins.

settings.summary: Drop tokens less likely than min-p times the likeliest (0..1, 0 = off).

settings.summary: Flat penalty on a token seen in the window (0 = off).

settings.default: the model file's sampling, else the engine's
settings.summary: Penalty growing with how often a token was seen (0 = off).

settings.default: the model file's sampling, else the engine's
settings.summary: Multiplicative penalty on seen tokens, must be > 0 (1 = off).

settings.default: the model file's sampling, else the engine's
settings.summary: The penalty window in tokens, 0..4096 (config.py caps at the engine's 4096-token window); sampling.md notes the effective default is 64.

settings.default: the model file's sampling, else the engine's
settings.summary: Fix the random draw; an integer (config.py accepts -2^63 to 2^64-1).
Undocumented in docs/configuration: in config.py's parser, runs a scripted engine instead of a model, for clients and tests (no model needed).
Undocumented: the mock engine's answer; given more than once, requests get them in turn and the last repeats.
Undocumented: tokenizer directory for the mock engine (a byte tokenizer if absent); relative to the config file.

Cards numbered as nvidia-smi, the first listed is the main card; "auto" takes every Blackwell card and makes the fastest the main; config.py also accepts a plain number or a list of numbers; gpus.md claims a server block works but config.py refuses gpu there.
VRAM the second card keeps free after its experts and prompt buffers, at least 128; raise it when the start says the peer's buffers do not fit.
Longest context in tokens; the KV cache grows with it; shared by parallel slots (each slot gets the total divided by N, floor 256, unless slot-full-context).

KV storage: Flash-Next takes fp16/int8/q4_0/k8v4 (int8 halves VRAM, q4_0 is 4-bit after rotation, k8v4 keeps K int8 and V 4-bit; not with kv-resident); DeepSeek takes fp8 (rounds as the reference) or fp16; a model refuses the other's values.

Keep N cells (at least 20,480) of KV in VRAM and the rest in pinned RAM; 0 = off; with parallel and int8 kv every slot streams its own K/V this way (the minimum is enforced by the engine, not config.py).
Extend RoPE past the trained length; fixed for the run.
The factor used by rope-scaling linear and yarn.
Raw RoPE frequency base; leave at 0 unless you know it.
Raw RoPE frequency scale; leave at 0 unless you know it.
YaRN original training context, as in llama.cpp; 0 lets the model's own value stand.
YaRN extrapolation factor, as in llama.cpp.
YaRN attention factor, as in llama.cpp.
YaRN beta-fast, as in llama.cpp.
YaRN beta-slow, as in llama.cpp.

settings.default: 700 (lowered to 300 on a card with too few slots)
settings.summary: VRAM kept free on the main card for graphs, scratch and the head; at least 256 (128 on Linux); raised to the floor the kernels need.
Keep experts the GPU does not hold in page-locked RAM; falls back to a file mapping when RAM is short.
At most N GiB of experts in RAM, hottest first; auto picks free RAM above the safety floor, capped at what the GPUs do not hold (this is the 'resident' amount of the automatic settings).
Use a file mapping for the experts instead of the RAM copy.
One shared file for the resident arena across processes (put it on /dev/shm on Linux).
The profile file deciding which experts start in VRAM.
Save the learned placement on exit and periodically, and start from it; needs the adaptive tier; a continuing workload starts right, a different one starts wrong.
The profile save period, in minutes.
With mmap-experts: keep the RAM-resident experts in ordinary RAM.
Hold the expert cache in segments so POST /v1/vram can lend VRAM between requests.
Segment size in MiB for the vram-elastic expert cache, at least 64.
Expert blobs kept in VRAM: auto takes what fits after weights, session and reserve, else an explicit count.
RAM left free for the rest of the system; the expert tiers take what is above it and the serving RAM guard holds it; 0 keeps nothing and turns the guard off.

settings.default: 1 on a server, 4 with a layer split (0 = off)
settings.summary: One adaptive round every N decode windows; fewer, later rounds cost less link but a topic change waits N windows.
Most experts one round swaps into the main GPU; bigger rounds catch up faster and move more bytes (the RAM copy keeps four times N free places).
Most experts one round swaps into the peer card; 0 freezes the peer tier.
Factor applied to routing counts after each round: lower follows topic changes sooner, higher keeps a long-run placement.

Automatic (Flash-Next): on only with a peer card, when the full expert set does not fit in free RAM but the set without the peer's share does; switching it on also turns off the cross-card prompt split (gpus.md).
CPU expert-pool affinity; the engine picks it when left out and a given value always wins; the docs give no value set beyond auto.
CPU expert-pool workers; auto is physical cores minus the host thread (on hybrid CPUs, P-cores minus one plus half the E-cores); a given value always wins.
Prompt chunk size: auto, auto:N (N = 8192, 16384 or 32768) or a plain token count.
Share of streamed prompt experts the CPU computes; fixed, so output is the same run to run.
A fresh part of at most N tokens is read through decode windows.
Run every row through every layer: slower, the same math.
The peer card computes none of the prompt rows; the prompt stays on the main card.
Verify windows of at most N tokens; 0 or 1 turns drafting off (the start line reports the window the engine actually runs).
Experts each drafter stage keeps (0 = all 128).
Prompt lookup drafting: fill a window from an earlier repeat of at least N tokens.
Caps the MTP drafter's own windows; 0 means 'use spec'.
The drafter attends to the last N cells of KV.

true or 0 to 1; CHANGES OUTPUT: under sampling keeps a draft the model gives probability P or more (greedy, logit_bias, JSON and tool calls stay exact; unless this is on, output is exactly plain decoding's); per request, relaxed_drafting: false or 0..1 forces exactness.
true or 1 to 9; CHANGES OUTPUT: skips experts no GPU holds when they rank R or lower in every window entry; needs the device MoE tail.
true or 0 to 16; CHANGES OUTPUT: adds LAMBDA to held experts' router logits; needs the device MoE tail.

Serve N requests at once (1..8, config.py PARALLEL_MAX = 8); it sets the engine's --batch/--slots and stops the start if either is set as well; max-context is shared per slot unless slot-full-context, and the slots' KV comes out of the expert cache.
The engine's batch width: parallel sets this for you, and basalt stops the start when parallel and batch are both given. Leave it empty unless you are driving the engine by hand.
The engine's slot count: parallel sets this too, and basalt stops the start when parallel and slots are both given. Leave it empty unless you are driving the engine by hand.
With parallel, give every slot the whole max-context, at N times the KV cache.
Conversation checkpoints kept, about 118 MB of RAM each; 0 reads every prompt from the start.
Also checkpoint every N freshly read tokens (RAM only).
Checkpoint the end of the system prompt when it is at least this many tokens long.
The token id that opens a chat turn; checkpoints go at the last one.
A short trailing turn that opens with this token id keeps the checkpoint in front of it; -1 turns it off.
RAM budget in MiB for parked conversations, 0 = off.
Most parked conversations.
Physical RAM kept free when parking conversations.
Park only conversations of at least this many tokens.
Disk budget in MiB for parked conversations; across a model swap, RAM conversations are written to disk at exit only when this is on.
Another folder for the disk tier; two models may not share one conversation folder while the disk tier is on (server.py).

Image input: off, dynamic (encoder inside the engine, borrows expert-cache slots on the main GPU, no standing VRAM), cpu (slow, no VRAM) or a GPU number running the sidecar on that card (about 2.2 GiB of its expert cache); config.py accepts the number as JSON number or string; needs a model with a vision projector; 32 MiB and 64 megapixels per image.

Allow http(s) image URLs on exactly this HOST or HOST:PORT from other machines (repeatable); a name must resolve to public addresses, an IP is taken as written; setting it needs vision on (server.py).
Allow image files (paths / file: URLs) under these directories from other machines (repeatable); relative paths resolve against the config file (config.py CONFIG_PATHS); setting it needs vision on.
Treat this machine's requests as remote too (for servers behind local forwarders): only data: URLs and what image-url-host / image-dir allow.
A GGUF control vector added to the residual stream at scale 1; a request switches it with experimental_speed_projection.
Control vectors with their scales, spelled FILE:SCALE[,...].
The layers the vectors apply to, inclusive ("A B"; in a file, a list of the two numbers, since engine values are passed one word each).
add: h += s v; project: h -= s (h.v) v.
Each layer's own direction, or single:L uses layer L's direction everywhere.
Engine flag (diagnostics page): the end-of-turn token ids; a list of numbers in the file.
Serve flag (diagnostics page): GPU stage times per request; not for A/B timing.
Serve flag (diagnostics page): show host wait times in the decode loop.
Serve flag (diagnostics page): one line per request on where decode time went.
Serve flag (diagnostics page): write one line per verify window (width, accepted, time) to this file.
Engine flag (diagnostics page): read the n-gram table unbuffered (direct) or lock it in RAM (ram).
Engine flag (diagnostics page): n-gram table row cache size, in rows (also a test knob).
Engine flag (diagnostics page): outstanding n-gram table reads (also a test knob).
Engine flag (diagnostics page): injected read delay in microseconds, for tests.

Diagnostic (docs/configuration/diagnostics.md): the RAM expert tier, for fixed-placement runs (the docs pair it with --diag-tier-frozen, which this 0.3.2 engine does not have). Not something to run a server with.
Diagnostic (CLI and serve): the card the DeepSeek drafter runs on.
Serve flag (diagnostics page): scheduling test on a card that cannot hold every expert; the output is wrong by design.
Serve flag (diagnostics page): base file for ppl= requests.
Serve flag (diagnostics page): where ppl= requests write rows.
Experiment keys, NAME=VALUE,... pairs per diagnostics.md; no stability promise, they go away with their experiment.
